newsitem.title: UK: JGBs take the lead in quiet week for bonds-Salomon.
newsitem.headline: JGBs take the lead in quiet week for bonds-Salomon.

text.p: Japanese government bonds (JGBs) took pride of place in the Salomon Brothers world government bond index (WGBI) for the week that ended on Thursday, Salomon Brothers said on Friday.
Overall the WGBI offered investors gains of only 0.06 percent.

JGB futures rallied during the week to close at their highest level for almost four months on Thursday, despite an International Monetary Fund report saying it would probably be desirable for Japan to begin raising interest rates later in the year.
JGBs made gains of 0.30 percent in yen terms.
For European bonds fortunes were mixed with French OATs making a respectable 0.23 percent in local currency terms and Italian BTPs and German Bunds gaining 0.12 and 0.11 percent respectively.
But British gilts posted losses of 0.12 percent in sterling terms.
U.S. Treasuries were also loss-makers this week, showing a 0.10 percent decline.

In dollar terms, continental European bonds offered the greatest value, the best being French OATs which gained 1.84 percent. Next came Belgium with a rise of 1.69 percent while Dutch bonds gained 1.64 percent.
Losers were gilts and Canadian and Swedish bonds.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
